# Gradient Components attribution

Charta's `gradient-components.css` adapts the vanilla CSS gradient line, divider, border, and underline primitives from **Gradient Components**, authored by **Alex Puliatti**.

- Source: https://github.com/alexpuliatti/gradient-components
- Revision: `4ba7a657985e898f3a96767ebdcea5a9ce488d83`
- Original stylesheet: https://github.com/alexpuliatti/gradient-components/blob/4ba7a657985e898f3a96767ebdcea5a9ce488d83/src/index.css
- Declared license: **MIT**, in the upstream [package manifest](https://github.com/alexpuliatti/gradient-components/blob/4ba7a657985e898f3a96767ebdcea5a9ce488d83/package.json) and [README](https://github.com/alexpuliatti/gradient-components/blob/4ba7a657985e898f3a96767ebdcea5a9ce488d83/README.md).

The inspected upstream revision supplies no separate LICENSE file or copyright notice. This attribution preserves its supplied author, license declaration, source, and revision without inventing an upstream notice.

Charta adapts the CSS primitives to its static HTML interface, dark palette, accessible interaction states, and reduced-motion behavior. Folder navigation uses the gradient-line base and vertical taper for its trunk; an open, rounded border mask extends the same gradient-line primitive to curved branches. The lines use the shared palette, brighter hover/focus/active states, and no continuous animation. It does not include the upstream React components, Framer Motion dependency, demo application, or remote font import.

Puliatti.com, Flywheel, and Orbserve inform the visual design. Their application code and assets are not redistributed here.
